Advect’s conventions fit treams-rs with a few release-dependent differences.

Proposal Timing
Scope CI badge to ?branch=main&event=push, matching Advect. Next README revision
Keep /latest/ documentation links and Documentation, Issues, Repository metadata URLs. Already aligned
Add PyPI version and Python-version badges. After first PyPI publication
Add Codecov’s main badge. After a successful coverage upload
Keep MIT badge; retain collective contributor credit and the treams paper. Already appropriate
Omit Advect’s conda badge and logo/centered HTML. No corresponding distribution or asset required

Sources: Advect README.md and pyproject.toml, clean at d5f4bae154f040f1e80c32dc7c1aab41e4c155dc, matching live public GitHub main. Compared against treams-rs README.md and metadata, clean at 99895b0f732effeac78041e16c4fb521b9f87b6f (condensed into a6b4f17).

Live checks: treams-rs PyPI JSON and /latest/ docs both return 404; Advect docs return 200. Therefore treams-rs’s install command and “documentation lives” wording remain prepared release text. […]

items.html:
The required Summary, Linked issue and Checklist sections are present. The draft clearly separates local validation from hosted checks and publication.

Two improvements:

  1. Replace “completes the unfinished work” with “resolves the remaining integration work” to avoid implying that release qualification is already complete.
  2. Replace “an original DLMF implementation” with “an independent implementation of the published DLMF formulas.” This distinguishes the implementation’s authorship from the mathematics.

Read-only review; no edits, tests or remote actions.
